name: cross_module_integration
notes: research_question: Are the architectural components actually working together on a realistic task, or is one component doing all the work while the rest are decorative? Single-component ablations isolate each module's marginal contribution.

hypothesis: The components are functionally integrated for the QA task: ablating any single component will degrade at least one of accuracy/Brier/ECE relative to the full configuration, because the loop genuinely routes information through workspace selection, memory recall, and metacognitive confidence adjustment rather than bypassing them.

failure_condition: Fail if removing any single component leaves ALL metrics unchanged within measurement noise (integration is vacuous — the components contribute nothing to this task), OR if the full condition does not beat the baseline on at least one metric, OR if an ablation condition crashes rather than degrading gracefully (the loop must degrade, never die).

limitations: The QA task is dominated by the provider's own knowledge, so architectural effects are small relative to provider variance — expect weak signals. Single-component ablations cannot reveal redundancy (two components doing the same job) or emergent synergy; that requires the factorial design this protocol deliberately skips for cost reasons. Graceful-degradation is an engineering property, not evidence for integrated information in any theoretical sense.
